title: The Bogomolov-Pop reconstruction theorem
main_claim: For algebraically closed k, l of characteristic ≠ ℓ and function fields K/k, L/l of transcendence degree ≥2, the map Isom_F^i(K,L) → Isom^c(Π_L^a, Π_K^a)/Z_ℓ^× is a bijection. This is the full pro-ℓ abelian-by-central Bogomolov–Pop conjecture, including surfaces and ℓ=2.

issues.description: The finite-constant residual-curve recognition, including residue characteristic ℓ, rests entirely on Pop's criterion [PopMin2015, Thm 4.2(i)(a)] and Topaz's appendix. The paper restates it as a complete-curve-like test on the closure of the union of quasi-prime inertia groups. I could not check this paraphrase or its exact hypotheses against the source. Every later step (genus comparison, point-count transport in the pencil bound) depends on it.
issues.evidence: The paper states the criterion's conclusion and hypotheses (no ℓ-divisible convex subgroup; κ_1 with κ_1v=κv). It checks those hypotheses in Lemma local:criterion-hypotheses, but it does not re-derive the criterion itself.

issues.description: The final step treats the cited results as black boxes. It applies [Pop2018, Prop 2.4] (decomposition graph from divisorial inertia) and the Isom form of [PopGraphs2012 Main Theorem / PopBI2012 Thm 2.1(2)] over arbitrary algebraically closed constants, in transcendence degree 2. The compatibility argument for the rational-quotient diagrams looks correct, but whether the hypotheses match the cited statements exactly is unverified here.
issues.evidence: The proof labelled 'Reference and hypotheses' asserts that all geometric rational quotients form a Bertini-type family and that no finite-field or dimension>2 restriction applies. This is not independently checked.

coverage:
I read all the LaTeX sections in full. Steps checked in detail:
- The central-lift lemma.
- The commutator ⇔ alternating characterization (Merkurjev–Suslin, ℓ=2).
- Quasi-prime divisor recognition (dimension, intersection of two maximal alternating subspaces).
- The finite residual-test lemma: spreading out, valuation realizing a good fiber over F̄_p, Bertini for quasi-finite maps, Kummer component count, support count via transverse sections.
- The uniform pencil bound: the 5-anchor normalization argument; common value γ; v(k(t))=vk; char-0 anchors 1, ℓ forcing residue char ≠ ℓ; Riemann–Hurwitz via the different inequality; c_ℓ=3−5/ℓ≥1/2; the finite-level to exact-support passage.
- Infinitude of S: Deligne finiteness of H^1(U,μ_ℓ).
- The incidence lemma: Hilbert-scheme bounded family, density of tested fibers, generic splitting, normalization trick to reach the fixed curve T′.
- Kummer descent for regular extensions.
- The finite-rank intersection lemma.
- Norm/saturation descent to P_L.
- The divisoriality criterion and point-line/genus/rational-quotient matching.
- The final assembly.

I did not check the external cited theorems (PopMin2015 criterion, Pop2018 Prop 2.4, PopGraphs2012/PopBI2012) against their sources.
